collection.credit:
NEW EVENTS - LIVING CULTURE III: DEFENSE, RAIDS AND THE FALLEN (LCC-01..50, draft, 2026-11-18)
"If anyone comes to raid our homeland, we'll be ready." Isola's people are peaceful but no pushovers: stamping dances and war chants, watch fires and plans, raids fended off or not, prisoners and bargains, and how the village honors those who defended it.
Written in the style of the owner's own events. The owner waived the review ("I'm sure the draft events are fine"); every event passed the Isola rules and the final 15-point review, logged in the notes.

collection.description: Raiders are camped in the forest: ambush them at dawn, or surround them and demand they leave.

setup.name: The setup
setup.text: (third) has found the raiders' camp in the forest, half a day's walk from the village: a dozen of them, sleeping by a fire, with the village's stolen pigs. (subject) wants to ambush them at dawn and finish it. (friend) wants to surround the camp and give them a chance to leave. What should the warriors do?

choices.label: Surround Them and Demand They Leave

o1.name: Outcome A
o1.text: The warriors fall on the camp at first light. It is over fast and it is not pretty: shouting, scattering, a spear thrown and a spear returned. The raiders run for the shore. (third) takes a blow to the head and does not remember the walk home. The pigs are recovered, most of them.

o2.name: Outcome B
o2.text: The warriors surround the camp in the dark, and at dawn (friend) stands up and tells the raiders, loudly, that they are outnumbered and should go. There is a terrible pause. Then the raiders pick up their spears, back slowly to the shore and leave. They take two of the pigs. Nobody is hurt.
